articles.title: Approves Rs 10,000-cr SME Growth Fund
articles.description: New Delhi, Oct 6: The Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, on Tuesday approved the government’s commitment of Rs 10,000 crore towards the establishment of the SME Growth Fund (SGF) to provide direct equity investments to small and medium enterprises (SMEs) and help create a new generation of Indian companies capable of competing globally. The initiative is part of the measures announced in the Union Budget 2026-27 to provide equity, liquidity and professional support to the MSME ecosystem. The government said existing funds provide equity support to enterprises, but most focus on early-stage businesses and largely cover micro enterprises. A structural gap, it said, remains in the availability of growth-stage equity capital for small and medium enterprises. The SGF is aimed at catalysing growth-oriented capital for SMEs across manufacturing, services, technology, innovation-driven sectors and strategic value chains. The government said the initiative would address the financing gap faced by viable SMEs seeking to scale operations, innovate, expand internationally, adopt advanced technologies, undertake acquisitions and emerge as industry leaders. The fund will provide “patient growth equity capital” to high-potential SMEs with demonstrated business viability and scalability. A majority of the fund’s allocation will be directed towards small and medium manufacturing-focused enterprises. It will also consider SMEs operating in industrial clusters in Tier-II and Tier-III cities. By providing long-term capital, the initiative is expected to help Indian SMEs expand capacity, adopt advanced technologies, enter international markets, integrate into global value chains and undertake strategic investments. The government said the fund would help create a strong pipeline of Indian companies with the scale, innovation capabilities and competitiveness required to become champions in their respective sectors. Under the initiative, the Government of India will provide an aggregate commitment of Rs 10,000 crore to an Alternative Investment Fund (AIF) established under the SGF framework. The government said the fund would complement existing measures to strengthen the SME sector, including digitalisation initiatives, credit support mechanisms, ease of doing business reforms, public procurement reforms, startup promotion initiatives and production-linked incentive programmes. The SGF is also expected to support balanced regional industrial development by investing in industrial clusters, including those in Tier-II and Tier-III cities. Such investments, the government said, would strengthen local supply chains and generate quality employment opportunities. The initiative is part of the government’s broader effort to strengthen India’s entrepreneurship ecosystem, deepen the domestic capital market for growth-stage enterprises and advance the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047.

articles.title: Mann cries vendetta as CBI raids camp office among 8 locations in Pb & Chandigarh
articles.description: The CBI on Tuesday conducted coordinated searches at eight locations across Punjab and Chandigarh, including the camp office of Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann, in connection with the alleged “cash for postings and favourable tenders” scam. articles.title: Cabinet okays Rs10,000 cr SME growth fund
articles.description: The Union Cabinet on Tuesday allocated Rs10,000 crore to establish an SME Growth Fund (SGF) for direct investments in small and medium enterprises (SMEs).The fund, announced in the Union Budget 2026-27, is introduced with the aim of providing growth-oriented capital for SMEs and creating champion enterprises across manufacturing, services, technology, innovation-driven sectors, and strategic value chains. It will also consider SMEs operating in industrial clusters in Tier-II and Tier-III cities.The SGF is intended to address a gap in growth-stage equity financing for SMEs. Existing funds providing equity support largely focus on early-stage businesses and micro enterprises, the government said.Also Read: Tata Sons chairman outlines three steps for sustained economic growthIt will provide long-term capital to businesses with established operations and the potential to scale. The government expects the investments to help SMEs expand their manufacturing capacity, improve productivity, increase exports and participate in global supply chains.The government has also highlighted credit support, digitalisation, public procurement reforms, startup initiatives and production-linked incentive schemes as part of its broader measures for the MSME sector. The official release said the initiative will help SMEs scale operations, and invest in technology and manufacturing capacity.The government has previously introduced a slew of measures as well to help the SMEs. The PM Mudra Yojana (PMMY), introduced in 2015, offers institutional loans of up to Rs20 lakh for non-corporate, non-farm small and micro enterprises. The Trade Receivables e-Discounting System (TReDS), launched in 2017, is an online invoice-discounting platform that helps SMEs convert trade receivables into liquid cash.In another announcement, the Cabinet approved the setting up of an Integrated Transport & Logistics Authority (ITLA) as a Special Purpose Vehicle to strengthen "research, planning, appraisal, monitoring and impact assessment" across transportation and logistics.ITLA will operate as the ‘apex body for integrated transport and logistics planning, research, project appraisal and monitoring, policy support and data analytics’. It will prepare a comprehensive National Transport Master Plan with a planning horizon of 10 years or more, covering roads, railways, shipping and mobility.
